page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highmem-4-lssd is an x86_64 server instance belonging to the Network Optimized family, configured specifically for memory-intensive tasks that benefit from low-latency scratch storage. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs backed by 31.0 GB of system memory, giving an allocation ratio of 7.75 GB per core. The instance does not include graphical processing units or specialized hardware accelerators, focusing all host resources on general-purpose and memory-centric x86_64 execution.

Storage capabilities are anchored by an integrated 403 GB local NVMe solid-state drive, providing direct-attached storage without the round-trip latency overhead of standard network-attached block devices. The instance includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which means network routing to external networks requires private networking constructs or separately attached IP allocations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, bundling 403 GB of NVMe SSD directly with a 7.75 GB-per-core memory ratio provides high resource density for stateful applications without needing auxiliary storage attachments. Operating with dedicated vCPUs guarantees consistent compute performance without virtualization contention. The instance profile aligns with in-memory caching systems, transactional databases requiring high-speed local logging, real-time analytics nodes, and ETL staging workers.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highmem-4-lssd is a network-oriented virtual instance engineered for memory-dense and high-I/O applications. Powered by the x86_64 architecture, it provisions 4 dedicated vCPUs and 31.0 GB of RAM, yielding an elevated ratio of 7.75 GB of memory per core. The instance integrates a local 403 GB NVMe solid-state drive directly into the configuration, avoiding the network overhead typically associated with external block storage for temporary data operations. Accelerator hardware is absent, focusing host capacity strictly on standard compute tasks. In terms of resource efficiency, the combined allocation of high memory density and direct-attached NVMe storage supports workloads with demanding throughput requirements without needing separate provisioned volumes. c4n-highmem-4-lssd is technically structured for in-memory databases, key-value stores requiring fast write caches, transactional processing nodes, and intermediate data transformation pipelines.
